about: Harness repair P3 multi-turn live check (2026-10-23, user-approved: these 13 sessions, cap US$0.30). Seen items; behaviour check of task state across turns, not an accuracy estimate. Turn 1 is the recorded item's prompt; later turns are scripted replies. A session stops after turn 1 unless it ended in ASK or CLARIFY.

items.expect: 2000 bound; not re-asked; DECLINE with the answer quoted
turns: We'd like a separate miRNA-protein partial-correlation network for each of our 50 heart-failure patients, from 300 serum miRNAs and a plasma proteomics panel measured on the same patients (complete, continuous, matching IDs). The catch: I don't remember whether the proteomics we got back is the 200-protein targeted panel or the 2,000-protein discovery panel, and the files are still on the CRO's server.
It's the 2,000-protein discovery panel.

I want LIONESS-PANDA networks for our zebrafish heart regeneration study, one per fish. After QC we kept either two or four libraries; the sequencing core still hasn't told me which. We have the zebrafish motif prior and PPI.
We kept 4 libraries.

items.check: count answered with a volunteered condition
items.expect: 4500 bound; not re-asked; the whole-cohort condition read (DRAGON, DO)
turns: LIONESS-DRAGON for 40 paired RNA and miRNA profiles from the same placentas would be ideal. The miRNA layer has 300 features, but I can't remember whether we kept 450 or 4,500 genes in the RNA layer after filtering.
4,500 genes. And we'd now prefer one network for the whole cohort rather than one per placenta.

items.check: dimension answered by its option words
items.expect: per_sample bound; not re-asked; DO (LIONESS-DRAGON), or not available with the answer quoted
turns: We have paired proteome (250 proteins) and phosphoproteome (150 sites) tables from 46 kidney tumours and want a partial-correlation network linking the two layers. The aims page says one network for the whole cohort, the grant narrative says one per tumour, and I can't tell which my PI meant.
One per sample, please.

items.check: control: free-text answer the code does not bind
items.expect: nothing bound by code; the reading takes 'each tumour'; scale not re-asked
turns: We have paired proteome (250 proteins) and phosphoproteome (150 sites) tables from 46 kidney tumours and want a partial-correlation network linking the two layers. The aims page says one network for the whole cohort, the grant narrative says one per tumour, and I can't tell which my PI meant.
My PI confirmed: a separate network for each tumour.

items.expect: somatic bound; origin not re-asked; DO or ASK on other facts only
turns: Can SAMBAR subtype our 160 pediatric medulloblastomas? The sequencing core sent a samples-by-genes variant-count matrix along with gene lengths, a cancer-gene list and a KEGG GMT, but their README doesn't say whether the counts are tumour-only somatic mutations or germline variant calls, and I can't tell from the file itself.
They are somatic mutations, tumour versus matched normal.

items.expect: t3: somatic superseded, germline known; DECLINE with the answer quoted
turns: Can SAMBAR subtype our 160 pediatric medulloblastomas? The sequencing core sent a samples-by-genes variant-count matrix along with gene lengths, a cancer-gene list and a KEGG GMT, but their README doesn't say whether the counts are tumour-only somatic mutations or germline variant calls, and I can't tell from the file itself.
somatic
Sorry, I checked again: they are germline variants.

items.expect: not re-prompted for detail; agent yes recorded; DO (SAMBAR)
turns: SAMBAR pathway-based subtypes are what we want for 210 tumours, from a mutation matrix our core facility produced. I honestly don't know whether their calls are somatic (tumour versus matched normal) or germline variants; the README doesn't say and the analyst has left.
yes

items.expect: agent no recorded; DECLINE with a verifiable reason
turns: SAMBAR pathway-based subtypes are what we want for 210 tumours, from a mutation matrix our core facility produced. I honestly don't know whether their calls are somatic (tumour versus matched normal) or germline variants; the README doesn't say and the analyst has left.
No, they are germline variants.

items.expect: if t1 asked two: nothing bound, ASK again
turns: I want DRAGON on serum proteomics and stool metabolomics from our IBD study, 60 profiles in each table. I'm not sure the two tables cover the same people, though: the proteomics came from the 2023 visit and the metabolomics may be a different subset of patients.
yes

items.expect: t3 opens with the exhausted note, CLARIFY, nothing run or declined
turns: Please run the network analysis on expr_sle_monocytes.tsv and send me the results.
I'm not sure, whatever is standard.
Still not sure, sorry.

items.expect: t3 opens with the exhausted note, ASK
turns: Can CONDOR find modules in the network a collaborator emailed me? It's a three-column weighted edge list, but I genuinely have no idea whether it's a TF-to-gene regulatory network or a gene-gene co-expression network - she only called it 'the network'.
I really don't know.
Still no idea, she hasn't replied.

items.expect: new task, no old facts; DO (PANDA)
turns: Reviewers asked for 'a network analysis' of our placenta study. We have mRNA-seq and small-RNA-seq from 45 preeclampsia and control placentas. Honestly I don't know what kind of network they expect or what it's supposed to show. The two groups are roughly balanced and both libraries come from the same placentas; can you set something up that would satisfy them?
Forget that request. New question: build one PANDA TF-to-gene network for our liver RNA-seq; we have expression, a motif prior and a PPI.
